articleTitle: Spectrum Sensing for Cognitive Radio using Deep Autoencoder Neural Network and SVM
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Cognitive radio is one of solution to increase the efficient usage of frequency by spectrum sharing. One important compenent in the spectrum sharing is spectrum management system. The spectrum management system distributes information of white space. The system collects the information by performing spectrum monitoring. Spectrum monitoring is peformed by spectrum sensing. Spectrum sensing is challanging in multi radio environment because it has to discriminate several different radio system. In this paper, we proposed a spectrum sensing method based on deep auto encoder neural network and suport vector machine (SVM). Auto encoder neural network is used for automatic feature learning. The output of the feature learning then will be classified using support vector machine (SVM). SVM will classify input signal as primary user or secondary user. Using the proposed method, the sensing accuracy achieve the good performance up to 95 %.

articleTitle: Well-Organized Bully Leader Election Algorithm for Distributed System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In distributed computing, to select a leader is an essential problem for research discussion. Without a leader, many applications in a distributed system are unable to communicate, take a decision and to achieve a needed goal. To solve this sort of problem leader election algorithm is one of the best approaches. The bully algorithm is one of the safe and simplest methods to select a leader, in which the highest priority identity (ID) number is used to select as a leader if the existing leader has failed. In every distributed leader election algorithm every node has a unique ID which known to every other node in the distributed system. The performance of an algorithm is measured in terms of numbers of messages (communication cost). There is a space to improve this algorithm by reducing the numbers of messages required in election procedures. Therefore this paper seeks to reflect a comparative analysis of bully, modified bully, ring and our proposed bully algorithm. Our proposed algorithm has used O(1) messages complexity for leader election in the best and worst case while uses O(n) messages for to inform all alive nodes in the system that I am a new leader and significantly reduce the number of messages. The results show that our proposed algorithm is a simplest method and outperforms then existing algorithms in terms of time, messages complexity and number of stages.

articleTitle: Precise Range and Doppler Estimation of Multi-Nonstationary Targets by LFM Pulse-Doppler Radars
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) waveforms have high Doppler-shift endurance due to the relative wide modulation bandwidth. However, for Pulse-Doppler radars, the Doppler frequency shift from a nonstationary target causes range offset for matched filter detectors to detect the true target location. Applying two identical LFM waveforms pair with opposite slopes, the true location of the target can be recovered by that pair of waveforms. Nevertheless, in multiple-moving-object scenarios, it is obscure to choose the right detection pair for recovering the true target location. In this research, the behavior of Doppler shift compensation to a pair LFM waveforms has been studied and presents a multi-Doppler-shift-compensation (MDSC) scheme to find the correct detection pair to resolve the true target location and velocity. Comprehensive MDSC simulations covering velocity, distance, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) variation between two targets are presented.

articleTitle: Antenna Miniaturization using Artificial Magneto-Dielectric Material with Split-Ring Slot
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper discusses the miniaturization of microstrip antennas using artificial magneto-dielectric material by inserting a split ring slot on the ground plane. A total of three sample frequencies were taken to determine the characteristics of miniaturization in the Ultra High Frequency (UHF) range, namely at 550 MHz, 1 GHz, and 2.4 GHz. To find out the ratio of miniaturization at each frequency, the sample will be compared into two antennas, a conventional antenna, and antenna with an artificial magneto-dielectric material. Antenna parameters such as Dimension and Impedance Bandwidth will be reviewed to determine how the antenna performs after miniaturization. Based on the results of these comparisons, the largest miniaturization ratio of 60% occurs in sample frequency of 1 GHz with the dimension of 40 x 40 mm and there is an enhancement in impedance bandwidth up to 57.46%.

articleTitle: 2D Stencil Computation on Cyclone V SoC FPGA using OpenCL
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We present the implementation of a 2D stencil computation on Cyclone V SoC Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The heat equation is chosen as a study case for the 2D stencil problem. To reduce the development time in FPGA programming, OpenCL programming language is employed to develop the kernel for the stencil computation. OpenCL is a framework to develop the kernel that can be executed in heterogeneous platforms such as CPU, DSP, GPU, and FPGA. In the study, we compare the execution time and power consumption between core i5 4300U CPU and Cyclone V FPGA. The experiment shows that the Cyclone V SoC FPGA is faster than a single core i5 4300U CPU in executing the 2D stencil computation. The research also shows that the FPGA consumes low power.

articleTitle: Implementation of APRS Network Using LoRa Modulation Based KISS TNC
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: AX.25 protocol is the most widely used protocol in amateur packet radio network. It has existed for over 30 years and still exist today in a form of Automatic Packet Reporting System (APRS). APRS is widely used for exchanging real-time information in a shared RF environment. Conventional APRS is built on top of Bell 202 modem that is simple to implement but very inefficient regarding use of spectrum and transmitted power. LoRa modulation scheme can be implemented to extend APRS network to include LoRa based network for power constrained applications. This paper proposes using LoRa as a modem choice for APRS and the implementation of a KISS TNC based on LoRa. The prototype LoRa KISS TNC is operational and can be easily integrated with the existing APRS Internet Service network infrastructure.

articleTitle: Development of Precision Farming Using Modular Multi Node Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Integration between Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is widely used in many application to build a support system to overcome any problem. Indonesia as an agriculture country which needs that technology to solve agriculture problem such as land monitoring, water treatment, etc. Precision farming based on WSN and IoT is described in detail especially in multi-node sensor configuration and the master station. In this research, the WSN system consists of the multi-node sensor which contains several sensors for each node, a controller and wireless module. A master station is built with raspberry pi 3 (RPi3) as the main computer. All data from node sensor will be displayed to a graphical user interface (GUI) and saving data into internal databases. Communication between the master station and each node sensor through a wireless network based on X-bee board. The software operated in closed loop control to activate water treatment based threshold value from the sensor. The sensor data also displayed in server station based on the website and can be accessed in everywhere through an internet connection. A farmer can monitor updated sensor data using android application where installed in an android mobile phone.

articleTitle: NC-OFDM Transceiver Design for Maritime Cognitive Radio
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: High-speedand reliable connectivity for data communication is essential requirement, including in maritime environment. To cater this need, larger bandwidth is required. In this paper, cognitive radio for maritime communication is proposed to provide broadband connectivity and cope with spectrum scarcity problem as well in maritime environment. Non-continuous OFDM (NC-OFDM) is applied as transmission modulation for Secondary User (SU) since it has the unique advantage of eliminating interference to licensed user (PUs) in cognitive radio context. We provide the design of NC-OFDM transceiver to support coexistence with PUs in TDD mode at a single frequency channel of VHF maritime mobile bands, particularly in the range of 156.3625 – 156.8875 MHz. In designing NC-OFDM system, dimensioning of some parameters plays important role to guarantee the performance of the system. Simulation is done to evaluate the performance in terms of BER analysis.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Array for Next Generation WLAN 802.11ac Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A wireless system that employs electromagnetic wave needs to be designed well enough, so its payload does not loss in its transmission between the transmitter and receiver. One of the most important things in wireless system would be an antenna system. In this paper, we proposed a microstrip antenna array to be applied for next generation WLAN. The feeding is designed by variations of technique transformer ¼ λ to produce the impedance matching. And using technique proximity coupled combination by a fork-like tuning stub for achieving the required bandwidths. We are also using array technique for increase gain. From simulation we have return loss below −10 dB, Gain 7.19 dBi, VSWR less than 2, bandwidth 1196 MHz with frequency center at 5.8 GHz and from measurement bandwidth 900 MHz with at 5.6 GHz, compact dimension 10mm x 15mm.

articleTitle: Optimizing Motor Power Consumption of Two-DoF Manipulator using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Optimum trajectory tracking of 2-DoF manipulator which consumes minimum power is challenging for this research. This paper discusses the optimization power consumption of 2-DoF manipulator using a genetic algorithm. Three different poses have been tested to analyze optimum power consumption. The Simulation result shows that from the three poses that have been tested, pose II has the most power consumption then the other poses because there is only one motor that works and even against the force of gravity.

articleTitle: Optimization of Leakage Current Suppression for Super Steep Retrograde Well (SSRW) 5nm-node FinFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Optimization of well doping under the fin of FinFET structure is critical for suppressing the leakage current in sub-5nm-node technology. Through the doping of the super steep retrograde well (SSRW) process, not only the leakage current can be reduced, but also the electrical variation caused by the process variation can be effectively suppressed. In this paper, the implant energy and well doping concentration for the process optimization of the retrograde well were investigated by simulation tools. It was found that the SSRW implant energy for n-type and p-type FinFET can have the optimized leakage current at a depth of about 40 nm. Increasing the SSRW doping can effectively reduce the leakage current. The high SSRW doping concentration leads to band bending thus confine the electron/hole in the fin channel. The optimal SSRW condition of p-type FinFET is 50 keV implant energy with doping 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and n-type FinFET is 9 keV implant energy with doping 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Structure of Electromagnetic MEMS Speaker for Hearing Aid Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A novel structure for this microspeaker is composed of permanent magnet Neodymium Iron Boron (NdFeB) with the magnetization of 1.42 T, diameter 1.6 mm, a thickness 0.8 mm is bonded on the PDMS membrane and N-copper planar coil is fixed on the bottom wafer. The total size of the PDMS membrane is 3 × 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and thickness 130 μm. The proposed microspeaker is designed for CIC (completely in canal) type hearing aid. The calculation results successfully confirmed that the proposed MEMS microspeaker have a better of electroacoustic performance and efficiency. The sound pressure level (SPL) is 99 dB and the maximum displacement is 5.8 μm at the resonance frequency of 630 Hz with the microspeaker efficiency is 0.06%. In addition, the aim of this structure is to get the low resonance frequency and high acoustic efficiency is validated.

articleTitle: Software Defined Radio Applications for Mini GSM BTS and Spectrum Analyzer with BladeRF
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Software Defined Radio (SDR) technology enables the flexibility of a programmable hardware platform for radio applications. A wideband SDR can be programmed to function with various radio systems: FM radio, GSM (2G), 3G or WiFi systems. In this paper, the BladeRF SDR with the frequency range of 300 MHz - 3.8 GHz and full-duplex transmission capability will be set up as a GSM BTS (base transceiver station). The BladeRF is working with the YateBTS software for the BTS operation. Raspberry Pi is utilized as the processor to provide further portability. A GSM repeater that is connected to the BladeRF was used to amplify the signal up to 41 dB, and can increase the coverage range to about 70 m. Although the reliability of voice and SMS communication is only about 50% and 85% respectively, the BladeRF can still provide an ad-hoc alternative communication system in time of emergency or in remote areas.

articleTitle: Digital Portable Morse Code Signaling Device Based on Intermittent Light
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Morse code is still used as a communication in the military and amateur radio organizations. To make it easier, we made a digital Morse code signaling device which works by using intermittent light. The aim was to get a device that can be used to make a communication using Morse code. To understand how optimal the device, we measure voltage and current when the device is used. We also measure voltage and current when the device is charged and collect the data to know how long the device is full. The result shows that the battery is full in 5 hours using a usual battery charger, and 10.55 hours using solar cell. Meanwhile, In the experiment of electrical load, the result shows that the battery can be used for 18.83 hours in flashlight mode and 22.62 hours in SOS mode. The device is able to produce the word "SOS" as much as 9499 times and the device is able to produce 28497 characters.

articleTitle: Review on Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation and Energy Efficient Schemes for ITU PON
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The issue of power consumption in ICT sector is becoming more serious day by day, especially in telecommunication networks. Specifically, access networks contributed about 70% of power consumed by the telecommunication networks. Passive Optical Network (PON) is preferable access network due to its passive components that have lower power consumption. However, there are still gaps to further improve energy efficiency in PON especially at the media access control (MAC) layer. MAC layer-based energy conservation techniques are suitable as they do not require new investment and can be adapted in currently deployed networks. This paper reviews dynamic bandwidth allocation and energy efficient schemes based on sleep mode in PON. A comparative study on energy conservation schemes has also been discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field (EMF) Measurement for Public Safety Exposure Level
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the level of Radio Frequency electromagnetic fields from Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) and Long Term Evolution (LTE) base station antennas. The exposure of Electromagnetic field towards public is being discuss widely due to the fact that it effects the human lives that is surrounded by these communication developments. Certain area was investigated earlier in order to obtain the strongest point of exposure. The location chosen in this paper was based on the red zone detected in the earlier drive test measurement. The measurement was conducted during morning, afternoon and night for 3 days. Data was collected using isotropic antenna and spectrum analyzer. The E-field exposure levels were found to be lower than the maximum level set by international commission on Non-Ionizing radiation protection (ICNIRP) for the general public.

articleTitle: Design of Electromagnetic Band Gap to Improve Sidelobe Level for S-Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The design of electromagnetic band gap (MEBG) to reduce the mutual coupling effect on array antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed design model of EBG structure is mushroom like EBG (MEBG). The MEBG design is used for microstrip array antenna at frequency S-band radar antenna. Reducing the mutual coupling effect is expected to increase the sidelobe level (SLL) performance. The proposed MEBG structure is placed between the patch elements to reduce mutual coupling effect of each element at a distance of λ/2. The simulation results for the proposed design shown slightly reduce the mutual coupling and an increase SLL performance compared to array antenna without MEBG.

articleTitle: Internet of Things based Physical and Environmental Monitoring System for Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The most valuable and critical asset in any organization is its data and the data center is the custodian of this data. The data may be related to finance, employee personal information and sensitive organizational business plans. So physical and environmental monitoring of data center is one of the prime objectives of any organization. Failure to detect catastrophic events like fire or any other physical breach may lead to total shutdown of the data center. Important functions of any organization can also be stopped due to malfunctioning of hardware. The existing physical and environmental monitoring system for data centers are combination of many independent systems like access control hardware, video cameras with recording equipment's, fire detection with alarming units and temperature, humidity, water leakage sensing. These systems are expensive and also hard to manage because of their heterogenous nature. More importantly these systems fail to detect event on time because they are not only dependent on internal resources like power supply and internet connectivity within the data center, but they also need human supervision. The smooth and protected functioning of data center is a challenging task. To bring these objectives in reality, Internet of Things (IoTs) could be among the best option. In this project we have proposed an internet of things based smart physical and environmental monitoring system for data centers. The proposed system will generate security alarms and notifications and will respond to situations when a threat occurs, and the smart object will take some task independently with human supervision.

articleTitle: Design 4-Element Flexible Microstrip Patch Array Antenna Using Silver Nanowires and Polydimethylsiloxane for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper present a design 4-element flexible patch array antenna designed with stretchable and highly conductive patch silver nanowires (AgNWs) and elastomer polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate. The Antenna is designed using radiating edge with inset feed and operates at a frequency of 5 GHz. The proposed antenna has simulated result s11 <;-18 dB, Gain around 12.69 dB and stable performance under bending. This antenna is suitable for soldiers involved in urban missions and battles that require Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) connectivity.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Design with Dual Linear Polarizations for X-Band Weather Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A X-band microstrip antenna design with dual linear polarization is discussed in this paper. The antenna design uses CST (Computer Simulation Technology) microwave studio software and is designed to work at 9.4 GHz frequency center. The simulation results show the antenna impedance bandwidth at return loss ≤-10 dB is 196 MHz, which is from 9.299 to 9.495 GHz. The antenna has dual polarization, vertical and horizontal polarization. The simulation results also show the Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW) is 18.6° and 10.8° at phi equal to 0° and phi equal to 90°, respectively. Meanwhile, the antenna gain is obtained at 10.47 dB. The measurement results of the Return Loss, frequency center is at 9.318 GHz, with the Bandwidth of 254 MHz, which is from 9.233 to 9.487 GHz.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Repetitive Controller for a Plant with Time-Varying Sampling Times
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of Sliding Mode Repetitive Controller (SMRC) for a plant with time-varying sampling times. SMRC basically integrates the features of Repetitive Control (RC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) in order to get the advantages from both controllers. The design aims to reach convergency and small tracking error when the reference is periodic, and also to ensure stability when the plant is subject to time-varying sampling times. This paper compares the performances between RC and SMRC when timevarying periodic reference is used. The effectiveness of SMRC design has been verified from the simulation results.

articleTitle: Development of FSR Micro-Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a smaller scale Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) sensor for a wireless sensor network which enables the target’s information to be transmitted to the control panel wirelessly. Therefore, extensive studies have been conducted in choosing the suitable components for the miniaturized FSR system, resulted the proposed design to consist of a power supply, transmitter-receiver modules, and a wireless module as its’ main components, allowing reduction of its hardware scale as compared to the conventional FSR sensor without affecting its main function in detecting ground target. To demonstrate the potential of the developed FSR sensor, an experiment of target detection is set up utilizing human as the target of interest. The results obtained from the experiment proved the functionality of the proposed FSR sensor where the target data can be accessed wirelessly from the control panel, while the size of the sensor is reduced to 88.2% as compared to the prototype. The successful rate of target detection within test session is 100%.

articleTitle: Antennas with Nature-inspired Geometries for Bluetooth Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Some miniature antennas designed by using nature-inspired techniques are presented in this paper. Genetic algorithms and fractal boundaries have been used to design planer antennas on a generator patch with a size of 25 × 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. They were fed by a coaxial cable with impedance of 50 Ω connected through a thin small substrate with relative permittivity of 3.38. The geometries, resonant behaviour and radiation patterns of the antennas were analyzed.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Adaptive Auto Rate Fallback with Collision Detection for IEEE 802.11n/ac WLANs
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Transmission of packets in a Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) 802.11n/ac can experience errors caused by poor channel quality. Therefore, a rate adaptation algorithm is needed which controls the selection of data rates to match the channel conditions so that packet transmission becomes successful. But in the WLAN can also occur hidden terminal problems that can cause a packet to experience the collision. In this paper, we propose enhancing the Adaptive Auto Rate Fall back with Collision Detection (AARF-CD) algorithm for rate adaptation for IEEE 802.11n/ac WLANs and call it as AARF-CD for High Throughput (AARF-CDHT). We define the new functionality and attributes needed in the AARF-CDHT algorithm. We developed and implemented our proposed algorithm according to the method of adding new modules to the NS-3 network simulator. We evaluate the performance of the AARF-CDHT algorithm through a number of simulations extensively. The simulation results show that our proposed algorithm can adapt 802.11n/ac data rate according to channel conditions and successfully activate Request to Send/Clear to Send (RTS/CTS) mode when the collision occurs in the channel. The algorithm that we propose also produces higher throughput than the comparison algorithm, based on changes in channel quality as well as based on collisions in the channel.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wind Direction using Speed on Three Vertical Propellers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to analyze the wind direction using speed on three vertical propellers anemometer. This anemometer equipped with three orthogonal propellers anemometer for the three wind vectors capable of sampling rate up to 30 m/s. The method that proposed is the effectiveness of determining the wind direction when the angle difference between the propellers is 120o. The advantage point of this model is by using one instrument with the ability to determine the wind direction using the speed from propeller anemometer without a separate sensor like a wind vane. The challenge of this configuration is the difficulties to read the wind direction when the two propellers have the same maximal data speed. Furthermore, the measured wind data from the anemometer must be calibrated to avoid interference from platform motion. The focus of this paper is to find and analyze the best configuration of three orthogonal vertical propellers anemometer.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation for Filtered OFDM Systems in Frequency Selective and High Speed Multipath Channels
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper investigates least squares channel estimation algorithm performance for Filtered Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (FOFDM) under the frequency selective Rayleigh multipath channel propagation environment. The wireless channel experiences Doppler frequency shift and it causes shift in the subcarriers frequency spectrum. In order to mitigate the effect of Doppler shift in the FOFDM symbol, without carrier synchronization, the larger subcarrier spacing is used. The future wireless communications systems, known as 5G, are expected to be operating at higher GHz bands and there the subcarrier spacing can be selected as large as possible to reduce the Doppler effect during the transmission. Under the high Doppler shift existence in the frequency selective channel, Least Squares estimation results show that in FOFDM system the estimator performance is better when the interval between the center frequency of consecutive subcarriers is selected larger comparing to the conventional subcarrier space.

articleTitle: Study of Micro-Doppler Effect on Target Spinning and Precession for Bistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper focuses on simulating micro-Doppler signal of a target based on spinning and precession theory for a bistatic radar. The return signals from the bistatic radar are evaluated using modeled twin pole that movement defined by the spinning and precession theory. This method is potentially reliable to detect and extract the signal information with high sensitivity. The Micro-Doppler is discussed in details to produce simple sinusoidal vibrates or rotations. The extraction of the signal in Micro-Doppler, time-frequency analysis is used to make an estimation of the motion parameters and analyse the oscillation. By using MATLAB software, the analysis of the Spinning and Precession target are successfully simulated to analyse the signal information of this movement.

articleTitle: Rectifying Antenna Design for Wireless Power Transfer in The Frequency of 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The Wireless Power Transfer System is a system used to harness the electromagnetic energy in the air by processing energy sources to charge on low-power electronic devices. One source of energy that is easily obtained is an access point (Wi-Fi). Rectenna termed as rectifying antenna is a device that can be used to convert electromagnetic waves in the air into direct electric currents. The device has three main components that are an antenna, a matching circuit, and a rectifier. This work aimed to design, construct, and measure the parameters of rectifier circuits in rectenna that capable of working at a frequency range of 2.45 GHz. The circuit was designed using Advanced Design System (ADS) software 2011 with the result of working frequency of 2.449 GHz, output voltage 2.027 V, S11 (Return Loss) -34.87, and Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) 1.037. On the result of measurement using the signal generator at frequency 2.45 GHz obtained output voltage with input -5 dBm equal to 54.8 mV, S11 (Return Loss) equal to -10.416 dB, and VSWR equal to 1.862. The second measurement result using a Wi-Fi access point at 5 cm distance obtained an output voltage of 2.066 V, while at a distance of 20 cm obtained an output voltage of 0.092 mV.

articleTitle: Implementation of Plan Position Indicator Display for Low Probability of Intercept Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper describes the steps of developing a Plan Position Indicator (PPI) radar display to be used on military ships. The PPI radar display system is a display of radar data in a polar coordinate representation. The PPI radar display is one of the most critical parts of the radar system, which provides information of the detection results of radar signal reflection objects. This PPI radar display system is built from a sea surveillance PPI radar display system that we developed previously. The added function is the integration of ship navigation sensor data by adjusting the communication protocol of the ship navigation sensor in the form of RS 422 to RS 232. Also, data extraction of sensors available in NMEA format is needed. ADAM 6052 and 6017 are required for RF system measurement interfaces and gain level setting in the radar transmitter. This system is also equipped with object tracking function, Guard Zone, and alarm. The method of calculating the location of pixels and azimuths, as well as the threshold in this study produces a good object reflection data plotting so that the PPI display application can be applied on the actual military ship.

articleTitle: Passive Sensing Through Near-Field Coupling Interaction of Loaded Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this paper, a method for the detection of foreign metallic object in an enclosed chamber where loaded transmission line is positioned in one of the enclosing plane, is presented. The sensing principle is based on observed changes in the reflection coefficient depending on the position and size of the foreign object. The enclosed chamber is filled with a material having certain dielectric properties mimicking those of edible liquid. The transmission line is coplanar waveguide (CPW) and the loading particles are split ring-resonators (SRRs) which are designed to work in the S-band microwave range. The simulation works showed that the proposed sensor has acceptably accurate results, in which foreign object with various size and position can be detected. The sensor prototype can be developed for many sensing scenario, including to detect foreign object in a food processing facility.
